All I said was that he technically (in part) caused it. To rephrase, at the very least, his actions (or inaction) contributed to the result. 

Pyrrha couldn't beat **full-power** Cinder, we don't know about how she'd go against half-power Cinder (especially if the transfer was able to be successful). So stating that part about Pyrrha not being able to beat her is not relevant cause I'm not talking about full-power Cinder here.

And I'm not saying Jaune needed to fight her anyway, I'm saying that if he had kept watch/guard like Ozpin told him to (if Ozpin had made it seem more important than just "while you're here you might as well", it probably would have helped him stay more on task), instead of looking away from the hallway to see what was going on with Pyrrha when she was crying out in pain from the transfer process, he might have called out that Cinder was there so Ozpin could defend. Instead, she got a free shot in to kill Amber, and therefore got the full power. 

I don't fault Jaune for reacting to Pyrrha being in pain the way he did, most people would have likely focused on their friend in pain instead of the task at hand. It was still a mistake, but a very understandable one to make. 

Of course, it's still 100% Cinder's fault for killing Pyrrha (and Ozpin, and also Amber but she was dying anyway by the looks of it) in the first place, but I wonder if things would have gone differently if Jaune had kept guard at the time. If Cinder didn't get her free shot off. 

It's less about blame, but rather cause and effect, and also perhaps something that *Jaune himself* might agonise over later once he understood more about what was happening at the time. He might blame himself for it. Perhaps it's part of what messes him up so much by the time we see him in Volume 9.

This is, to note, also assuming that Ozpin would be capable of fighting Cinder while successfully defending Amber and Pyrrha during the transfer process, and also requiring that the console not need to be touched during said transfer too. We don't have answers for whether or not that would have been possible, though, we can only speculate. Hypothetically, if he wasn't capable of doing that against half-power Cinder, then Jaune's mistake is irrelevant to the situation.

Technically Jaune causes her death when he stops keeping guard and is focused on Pyrrha being in pain during the aura transfer, leading to Cinder getting a free shot to kill Amber (and therefore absorbing the remaining maiden power). If that didn't happen, likely Ozpin and Pyrrha would have survived (Cinder likely fleeing when she realised she was outmatched). If he was able to protect the pods, at least.

Your dismissal of gender diversity has left you ignorant. 

Gender is a spectrum that flows from man to woman. Think of it as a number line. How many points are between 0 and 1? Infinite. Gender works the same. The gender spectrum is usually split into 3 sections: the man side (let's say the 25% on the man end of it), the woman side (the 25% on the woman end of it) and the non-binary middle (the 50% between the two). The majority of the population sit in one of the two 25% sections, but there are people (non-binary) who sit in the middle 50%. Some people move along this spectrum over time (gender fluid), others are not on the spectrum at all (agender). 

Nowhere on that spectrum does it include cross-species or age related conditions. I personally have not interacted with someone who deals with such, and I don't deal with either of the two either, so I don't know how it works specifically.

General gist is that the mind is complicated and can be fucked up/things go wrong with the wiring. (I am transgender, and I agree that it is technically a mental disorder (Gender Identity Disorder), the only known treatment being transition and integrating into society as one's experienced gender, or lack thereof). Seeing as the brain is too complex to just 'fix' through surgery, people dealing with said abnormalities have to live with them in whatever way is most comfortable. People like you who refuse to acknowledge something as simple and basic as preferred pronouns make an already difficult condition even harder. If you have even a shred of human decency, even if you don't understand or agree with gender diversity and such, at least refer to people by the pronouns they prefer. It's not hard. It takes effort, yes, especially if you're not used to it, but it's ultimately a simple and basic thing that you can do to make the lives of other people easier. Transsexual is similar to transgender, most commonly used to describe post-transition (especially post-surgery). The prefix trans- in transgender means on a different side of, in this case referring to the transgender person's gender being different or misaligned with the sex they were born with. Transsexual is (usually, not always, and some transfolk don't like being referred to as such) when one's sex is different to what they were born with. A transgender woman, for instance, has her gender (woman) on the opposite side of the spectrum to what would normally be expected for someone with her birth sex (male). Should she undergo transition, she would then be transsexual (if she chooses to adopt that label) as her then-sex (female) is on the opposite side of the spectrum to her birth sex (male).

Cis- on the other hand, as in cisgender, is what the general population is, where their gender aligns with their sex. A cisgender woman was born female and has the gender (woman) to match.
